messages:
erin.w: heads up — customer 'acme' reported burst 429s last night (18:20-18:45 UTC). They say project 'acme-prod' shows <10% usage in the console, but their app hit intermittent 429s and degraded UX. attaching snippet from their logs.
support-bot: created ticket #ACM-3456 and linked to customer conversation :ticket:
sam.ops: can you paste the raw request/response headers (especially X-RateLimit-* and x-request-id)? also their public egress IP if available.
erin.w: pasted what they sent:
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer key_prod_ABC123" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
x-ratelimit-limit: 100
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 1670001200
x-quota-scope: org:acme
```
They also said they call from a NATed IP (203.0.113.45) shared across a few tenants in their k8s cluster.
mike.eng: quick notes from infra: our throttling/rate-scope precedence is intended to be: API key -> project -> org -> IP. If a request includes a key mapped to a project, we scope against project quotas first. If key has no explicit project, it should fall back to org. IP quotas are only consulted when requests are unauthenticated or flagged as proxy-only. That said, we recently shipped a routing tweak for multi-auth where we normalize auth principals — I wonder if customer hit the edge-case where key didn't carry project metadata.
jane.ps: NATs + shared infra can complicate heuristics. If their key is being rotated or they use multiple keys, our backend might have intermittently written an empty project field for the authorization principal. That would make the request evaluate against org quota (which they said is low) — but why x-ratelimit-remaining=0 while console shows slack usage? :thinking:
mike.eng: digging in logs for x-request-id rq_0a1b2c3d — found entry. TL;DR: routing bug where, for a small window during a config rollout, project metadata was dropped for keys created before the rollout. That left the request principal `org:acme` only. Because the customer shares the NAT with other tenants, during a concurrent burst the IP-scoped aggregated counters tripped a guard that has lower threshold for unauthenticated-ish principals. In short: key lost project mapping -> counted against org & ip windows -> hit 429.
erin.w: ok — can you provide repro steps I can run or give the customer so they can validate? they want to test immediately before we ship a fix.
mike.eng: repro steps (safe, non-prod):
1) create two keys in same org, one with explicit project `acme-staging` and one older key without project metadata.
2) from one machine (simulate NAT), fire concurrent requests with the old key at ~250 RPS for 30s:
```
ab -n 5000 -c 100 -H "Authorization: Bearer key_old_XXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```
3) observe x-ratelimit-remaining go to 0 and 429s; then rotate to key with project and observe rate-limits apply at project level (higher headroom).

note: this only appears during config rollout windows; we have a patch ready to avoid dropping project metadata during transition and will backfill metrics for affected window.

workaround: re-issue the API key bound to a project or use a project-scoped key; alternatively, ask customer to route traffic through a dedicated egress (so NAT is not shared) until we deploy the patch.
sam.ops: patch is queued for canary tonight (22:00 UTC). engineering will monitor ACME org and post an update in this thread when done. :eyes:
erin.w: thanks — i'll relay repro + temporary workaround. i'll also ask for a quick confirmation once you roll the canary.
mike.eng: update: canary deployed at 22:12 UTC, observed no project-metadata drops in 15m window, increased headroom for acme during test burst. full roll to prod scheduled in 2 hours, will monitor for any remaining 429 traces and send a summary.
erin.w: perfect, i've messaged the customer with steps + temporary mitigation. marking high priority but not outage. will follow-up if they still see 429s. :raised_hands:
